- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for downward momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon; apply a 1–2% upward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- Sentiment spikes (≥0.5) in last 3–5 days correlate with price drop; if forecast is rising after such spike, reduce slope by 20–30%.
- If sentiment is flat (0.0) for 5+ days, model tends to drift downward; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to prevent premature decline.
